question: From T050.csv compute the signal-to-noise ratio as max(intensity in 990-1012 cm-1) divided by the sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of 1800-1900 cm-1. Both intervals are inclusive.
answer_text:
The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was calculated by identifying the maximum intensity in the region between $990$ and $1012\text{ cm}^{-1}$ ($999.046$) and dividing it by the standard deviation of the intensity in the background region from $1800$ to $1900\text{ cm}^{-1}$ ($\approx 6.284$).

import numpy as np

# The file contents are in 'files'
# Data from first provided file (T050.csv)

y = np.array(data['intensity'])

# Define ranges
sig_mask = (x >= 990) & (x <= 1012)
